title: Build a web app: a workout timer

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Without knowing a single line of code, you can describe an app to Claude and have your own app built. Today it's a workout timer.

  • Press start and a ring-shaped timer counts down,
  • and it reads out "three, two, one" for the last 3 seconds.

Preview the finished example ↗

  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 2, and a web browser like Chrome, Edge or Safari

steps.title: First, what's a web app?
steps.html:
A web app runs inside your web browser. No app store and nothing extra to install, which makes it the easiest kind to build first.

index.htmlA text file describing the app's screen and behavior. It's the web app's "front page", hence the name
HTMLThe language for what goes on screen (buttons, text, pictures)
BrowserA program for viewing the web, like Chrome, Edge or Safari. Open the file in it and it becomes an app

Claude writes the code. You just say what you want and check the result with your own eyes.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: Describe it and have it built
steps.html:
The more specific you are, the better it builds. Send the sentence below as is.

Permission cards appear for making a folder and a file. Check it's making index.html inside a timer folder, then click Allow. You don't need to understand the code.
steps.alt: A permission card for creating timer/index.html
steps.code: Create a timer folder and build a workout timer web app in it as a single index.html. A big start button, a 20-second ring timer, and read out 'three, two, one' in English for the last 3 seconds. Make it look good on a phone too.

check.q: Is there a timer folder with index.html inside your Practice folder?

steps.title: If no file appears, or it was built differently
steps.html:
• If you denied a card, send it again and allow it.
  • It's fine if it split things into several files (style.css, app.js…). You just need index.html.
  • If Claude asks you something, answer it. For example: "Use an English voice."

steps.title: Open it in a browser and try it
steps.html:
1. Open the Practice folder on your desktop → the timer folder.
  2. Double-click index.html and it opens in your browser.
  3. Turn your speakers on and press Start.

You can also tell Claude "Open index.html". A permission card for opening a program will appear.
steps.alt: A ring timer and start button in the browser

check.q: Did the timer count down, and did you hear "three, two, one"?

steps.title: If it won't open or there's no sound
steps.html:
• Notepad opens: right-click index.html → Open with → Chrome, Edge or Safari.
  • No sound: check your volume. Browsers only play sound after you press a button.
  • Blank or odd screen: take a screenshot (Desktop 7) and send it with "This is what I see. Please fix it."

steps.title: Change it with words
steps.html:
The real power of building apps this way is changing them with a sentence. Let's add rest time and rounds.

  1. Send the sentence below, check the changed lines (red and green), and click Allow.
  2. Go back to the browser and refresh. (Windows: F5 · Mac: Cmd+R)
Refresh to see the change. The file changed, but the open page doesn't update by itself.
steps.alt: A permission card changing the rounds and rest time
steps.code: Change it to 20 seconds of work and 10 seconds of rest, repeated 3 times. Make the timer green during rest

check.q: After refreshing, does it go work → rest (green) → work… 3 times?

steps.title: If nothing changed, or it broke
steps.html:
• Check you refreshed.
  • If it broke, say "Undo that last change." (Desktop 6)
  • If it's not what you wanted, say what's different and how. For example: "After the rest, the next round doesn't start."

steps.title: 🎉 App practice 1 done! Your own web app
steps.html:
You described an app, had it built, and changed it with words. That's the basic loop for building apps with AI.

Say what you wantcheck the cardOpen it in a browsersay what to changeRefresh

Things to try next

  • "Let me type in the exercise name"
  • "Play a clapping sound at the end"
  • "Keep a record of how many times I did it today"

Earlln's EarllnCore (a morning core workout app) started just like this and grew one sentence at a time.
